five days of low-grade fever and severe headache
Examination recorded marked meningeal signs; head CT showed no abnormality.
Initial cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) contained 183 cells/µL, 97.8% lymphocytes, and protein 83.3 mg/dL.
CSF PCR did not identify an infectious cause, and Borrelia serology was negative. No CSF culture result is supplied.
During that admission she received intravenous dexamethasone for nine days.
She improved and was discharged after 12 days on 11 March 2026.
Persistent headache and photophobia led to further emergency visits.
On 14 March she was readmitted with severe orthostatic headache, upper-limb tremor and dizziness.
Brain MRI was normal.
Repeat CSF contained 178 cells/µL, 97.7% lymphocytes, and protein 36.6 mg/dL.
